result.note: Tests the Electricity Act provision invoked and the key elements of the Ministry of Power's summer 2026 playbook.

questions.prompt: In March 2026, the Ministry of Power directed Tata Power's Mundra plant to start operating to prevent summer blackouts. Under which provision was this direction issued?
options: Section 3 of the Energy Conservation Act
Section 3 of the Essential Commodities Act
questions.explain: The government invoked Section 11 of the Electricity Act to force the 4,000 MW Mundra plant into action by 1 April 2026. The move was part of an emergency playbook to offset gas shortages caused by the West Asia conflict.
questions.source: The government invoked Section 11 of the Electricity Act to force Tata Power’s 4,000 MW Mundra plant into action by April 1

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the Ministry of Power's plan, announced in March 2026, to meet summer electricity demand:
items: Gas accounts for about 10% of India's electricity generation.
The Ministry is accelerating clearances to commission wind and battery energy storage systems.
Maintenance on thermal plants is being deferred to keep 10,000 MW on the grid.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: The first statement is wrong: gas provides only 2% of India's power, though it supplies 10 GW during peak demand or heatwaves. The Ministry is also pushing up coal inventory and tweaking rules to encourage industries to use captive power.
questions.source: Gas provides only 2% of India’s power, but it provides 10 GW during peak-demand periods or heatwaves.
